summary:
Mission Architect: Design. Explore. Discover.

Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based space exploration game developed by Team Axiom X to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and explorers.

Players take on the role of space mission engineers, designing spacecraft, managing resources and making critical decisions across three challenging missions: Mars, Europa and Saturn.

Through realistic engineering trade-offs, interactive navigation, scientific exploration and performance-based scoring, players discover how decisions involving propulsion, power, radiation protection and mission planning influence success or failure.

Inspired by NASA's space exploration missions, Mission Architect transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible, engaging and educational experience that encourages curiosity, creativity, critical thinking and problem-solving.
details:
Mission Architect: Design. Explore. Discover.

Team: Axiom X
Creators: Artin Mansouri and Mahoor Kiani
Project Type: Interactive Educational Space Exploration Game

1. The Problem

Space exploration is one of humanity's greatest scientific and engineering achievements. However, the complex decisions behind successful space missions are often difficult for students and the general public to understand.

Designing a spacecraft involves balancing competing requirements such as mass, cost, power, propulsion, fuel, communications, radiation protection and scientific objectives. A decision that improves one aspect of a mission can introduce risks elsewhere.

Although space missions capture the public imagination, many educational resources focus primarily on mission discoveries rather than the engineering decisions that make those discoveries possible.

Our challenge was to make space mission engineering understandable, interactive and engaging.

2. Our Solution: Mission Architect

Mission Architect is a browser-based educational game that allows players to experience the responsibilities of a space mission engineer.

Instead of simply watching spacecraft explore the Solar System, players design mission systems, evaluate engineering constraints, manage resources and respond to operational challenges.

The game features three progressively challenging destinations: Mars, Europa and Saturn.

Each mission introduces different environmental conditions, engineering trade-offs and gameplay mechanics. Players receive performance-based scores and medals reflecting their mission decisions and outcomes.

The central principle is simple:

Every engineering decision has consequences.

By combining scientific concepts with interactive gameplay, Mission Architect transforms complex aerospace engineering challenges into an accessible learning experience.

3. Three Missions, Three Engineering Challenges

Mission 1 — Mars: Design and Plan

The Mars mission introduces the foundations of spacecraft design and interplanetary mission planning.

Players configure their spacecraft by selecting scientific objectives, instruments, spacecraft systems, power sources, communications equipment and launch capabilities.

They then plan their journey using an interactive flight planner, selecting propulsion systems, transfer profiles, propellant mass and mission duration.

Additional decisions involve launch opportunities, battery reserves, communications modes, atmospheric entry and landing systems, solar panel conditions and science operations.

The game's engineering assessment evaluates the feasibility of these decisions using simplified educational models.

Key learning outcomes:

  • Understanding spacecraft mass, power and budget constraints.
  • Exploring the relationship between propulsion, fuel and mission duration.
  • Evaluating launch and landing risks.
  • Recognising how mission planning affects scientific success.

Mission 2 — Europa: Survive and Explore

Europa, one of Jupiter's icy moons, presents a different set of engineering challenges.

Players select scientific instruments to investigate Europa's icy surface, potential subsurface ocean and geological characteristics.

They must also choose spacecraft power systems, radiation protection, communications architecture, transfer strategies and exploration approaches.

The mission includes interactive spacecraft navigation through a simulated Jupiter environment, where players steer to avoid radiation hazards and collect scientific data.

Spacecraft shielding affects damage resistance, while operational decisions influence available resources and mission performance.

Key learning outcomes:

  • Understanding radiation hazards around Jupiter.
  • Evaluating spacecraft shielding and power-system trade-offs.
  • Exploring the importance of autonomous spacecraft operations.
  • Balancing spacecraft survival with scientific data collection.

Mission 3 — Saturn: Navigate the Rings

The Saturn mission focuses on spacecraft navigation, hazard avoidance and precision operations.

Players configure propulsion, shielding, sensors, transit speed, scientific instruments and power systems before beginning their mission.

During an interactive flight sequence, they navigate through simulated ring-particle hazards while monitoring spacecraft integrity and progress.

The mission also features a docking sequence, introducing the importance of controlled spacecraft manoeuvres.

Key learning outcomes:

  • Understanding navigation challenges in hazardous environments.
  • Evaluating the relationship between spacecraft protection, mass and manoeuvrability.
  • Exploring sensor-assisted hazard detection.
  • Recognising the importance of precision during spacecraft operations.

4. Engineering Mechanics and Scientific Principles

Mission Architect integrates several interconnected engineering concepts into its gameplay.

Spacecraft configuration: Players select equipment and mission systems, learning how each component contributes to overall spacecraft performance.

Mass and budget management: Engineering choices must be evaluated against practical resource limitations.

Power management: Different power systems introduce trade-offs involving reliability, availability and mission environment.

Propulsion and trajectory planning: Players explore how propulsion efficiency, propellant availability and transfer duration affect mission feasibility.

Radiation protection: The Europa mission demonstrates how shielding choices influence spacecraft survivability.

Navigation and risk management: Interactive flight sequences challenge players to avoid hazards while preserving spacecraft integrity.

Scientific operations: Instrument selection, data collection and communications decisions influence mission outcomes.

These mechanics use simplified educational assumptions rather than high-fidelity spacecraft engineering calculations. Their purpose is to demonstrate the relationships between engineering decisions and mission outcomes in an understandable way.

5. Educational Benefits and Impact

Mission Architect is designed to encourage learning through experimentation, decision-making and feedback.

Players can compare different spacecraft configurations, observe the consequences of their decisions and improve their strategies through repeated attempts.

The game promotes:

  • STEM engagement: Introducing aerospace engineering, physics and planetary science through interactive exploration.
  • Critical thinking: Encouraging players to evaluate competing technical requirements.
  • Problem-solving: Challenging players to respond to operational difficulties and unexpected hazards.
  • Systems thinking: Demonstrating how propulsion, power, communications, shielding and science systems depend on one another.
  • Learning through failure: Allowing players to understand why missions fail and how improved engineering decisions can increase their chances of success.

The browser-based format makes the experience accessible without specialised simulation software.

Mission Architect is intended for students, educators, space enthusiasts and anyone interested in understanding how spacecraft missions are planned and operated.

6. Technology and Development

Mission Architect was developed as an interactive web application using:

HTML: To structure the game interface, engineering configuration panels and mission information.

CSS: To create responsive layouts, visual effects, mission environments and spacecraft animations.

JavaScript: To implement gameplay mechanics, engineering calculations, mission events, scoring, spacecraft controls and progression between missions.

HTML Canvas: To support interactive spacecraft navigation and animated mission environments.

The application runs directly in a modern web browser without requiring users to install dedicated software.

The game combines interactive controls, visual feedback, resource indicators, mission assessments and animated sequences to connect engineering decisions with gameplay outcomes.

7. Innovation and Creativity

Mission Architect's central innovation is its combination of engineering decision-making with interactive space exploration.

Rather than presenting isolated scientific facts, the game places players in situations where they must apply engineering principles to achieve mission objectives.

Each planetary destination introduces a different challenge:

Mars tests mission design and planning. Europa tests resilience and scientific exploration. Saturn tests navigation and operational precision.

The progressive structure encourages players to develop their understanding of spacecraft engineering while experiencing increasingly complex mission scenarios.

By linking technical choices to visible outcomes, Mission Architect makes engineering trade-offs a central part of the game rather than background information.

8. Future Development

Mission Architect has the potential to evolve into a broader educational platform for space mission engineering.

Future improvements could include:

  • Additional destinations, including the Moon, Venus and other planetary moons.
  • More advanced spacecraft design and trajectory simulation.
  • Expanded scientific instruments and mission objectives.
  • Integration of verified NASA datasets and mission parameters.
  • Classroom learning modes with guided engineering challenges.
  • Additional accessibility features and educational explanations.
  • Expanded mission scenarios, achievements and performance comparisons.

A future version could also allow educators to customise mission constraints and use the game to demonstrate specific STEM concepts.

9. Conclusion

Mission Architect demonstrates how interactive technology can make space mission engineering more accessible and engaging.

By combining spacecraft design, mission planning, resource management, hazard navigation and scientific exploration, the game encourages players to think like engineers and understand the decisions behind space exploration.

Developed by Team Axiom X, Mission Architect aims to inspire curiosity, strengthen problem-solving skills and encourage the next generation to explore opportunities in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Mission Architect — Design. Explore. Discover.
